content: Before using zanamivir, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients, such as lactose or milk proteins, which can trigger allergic reactions or other complications. This medication may cause dizziness. Consuming alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) can exacerbate this effect. Avoid driving, operating machinery, or engaging in activities that require alertness until you are confident you can do so safely. Limit your intake of alcoholic beverages. Zanamivir may be less effective in young children. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used if clearly necessary. It is not known whether this drug passes into breast milk. Drug interactions can alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Maintain a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Inform your doctor if you have received a nasal flu vaccine in the past two weeks. If zanamivir is administered too closely to the nasal flu vaccine, it may interfere with the vaccine's protective effects. In the event of an overdose, if someone exhibits severe symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. This medication has been prescribed specifically for your current condition and should not be used as a substitute for the flu vaccine. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is within two hours of your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and proceed with your next dose at the regular time. Store this medication at room temperature in a dry place. Do not puncture the foil blister until you are ready to take your dose. Avoid storing it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. For flu treatment, inhale this medication through your mouth as directed by your doctor, typically two inhalations (one blister per inhalation) twice daily, approximately 12 hours apart, for five days. For flu prevention, inhale two inhalations (one blister per inhalation) once daily as directed by your doctor. Before use, remove the cover on the disk inhaler and check the mouthpiece to ensure it is clean and free of particles. Load the medication disk into the disk inhaler, puncture one medication blister, and keep the disk inhaler level to prevent spilling. Exhale completely through your mouth, place the mouthpiece into your mouth, and inhale deeply through your mouth to draw the medication into your lungs. Hold your breath for a few seconds. To take another inhalation, advance to the next medication blister and repeat the process. Begin zanamivir treatment as soon as possible. This medication works best when the amount of medicine in your body is maintained at a constant level. Continue using this medication for the full duration prescribed, even if your symptoms improve. If you have breathing problems, such as asthma or chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), and are scheduled to use inhaled bronchodilators (e.g., albuterol) at the same time as zanamivir, use the bronchodilator medication before using zanamivir. Dizziness may occur as a side effect. Additionally, because this medication is an inhaled powder, you may experience increased coughing after use. Remember that this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefit to you outweighs the risk of side effects. However, zanamivir can cause breathing problems, which in rare cases may be fatal. If you experience difficulty breathing, such as wheezing or shortness of breath, stop using zanamivir and seek medical attention immediately. Zanamivir is not recommended for individuals with lung or breathing problems. Discuss the risks and benefits with your doctor. The flu itself or zanamivir may rarely cause serious mental or mood changes, which may be more likely in children. A very serious allergic reaction to this drug is rare. This is not a complete list of possible side effects. In the U.S., contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for medical advice about side effects. This information is a summary and does not contain all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that this product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. This information is not a substitute for individual medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
